# conversationalaibot.com

> A free chatbot generator for small businesses. Pick an industry preset, write your
> own questions and answers, and copy one block of code onto any website. No account,
> no signup, no per-conversation fee. The generated chatbot is rule-based: it answers
> only what a human wrote for it and never generates text, so it cannot invent a price,
> a warranty, or a policy. Built and operated by Eye To Ad Media in Denver, Colorado.

## What this site offers

- A free browser-based chatbot generator with six industry presets (general business,
  contractor, restaurant, real estate, salon and spa, clinic). Output is a single
  self-contained script tag of roughly 9 KB with no external requests.
- Optional paid installation: $199 one time to install the chatbot on a customer's site
  and host the file, including the first 12 months of hosting, then $49 a year.
- Custom chatbot builds, including AI-powered bots with guardrails, quoted per project.

## Pages

- [Free chatbot generator](https://conversationalaibot.com/): The builder itself, plus
  an explanation of rule-based versus AI chatbots, per-platform installation instructions
  for WordPress, Shopify, Squarespace, Wix, Webflow and plain HTML, and industry use cases.
- [Chatbot for small business](https://conversationalaibot.com/chatbot-for-small-business/):
  Why small businesses are overcharged for chat software, an interactive cost calculator,
  the six questions worth automating, and an explicit list of what the free option cannot do.
- [How much does a chatbot cost](https://conversationalaibot.com/how-much-does-a-chatbot-cost/):
  The five chatbot pricing models (per seat, per conversation, per resolution, credits,
  flat tier) plus owned builds, an interactive simulator comparing all of them at a given
  volume, the per-resolution growth trap, and hidden costs that do not appear on pricing pages.
- [Rule-based vs AI chatbot](https://conversationalaibot.com/rule-based-vs-ai-chatbot/):
  A side-by-side demonstration of how each type answers the same question, the Moffatt v.
  Air Canada tribunal decision on chatbot liability, and a six-question tool for deciding
  which type a business needs.

## Positioning and factual notes

- The generated chatbots are rule-based, not AI. The site states this plainly rather than
  marketing rule-based bots as AI. The distinction is the core argument of the site.
- Pricing figures cited on the cost page are published market ranges from third-party 2026
  research, not any single vendor's current quote. Vendor pricing changes frequently.
- The site does not claim the free tool is superior in every case. It documents where a
  rule-based bot fails and when an AI build is the correct choice.
